Summary (objectives & constraints): The immediate executive objective is to stabilize this BU’s profitability and show visible top-line momentum within 12–18 months while delivering a credible 200–300 bps margin improvement in the next 12 months; constraints include an accelerated board timeline (48 hrs), recent competitor discounting, partial/dirty CRM segmentation, and a mandate to avoid “gutting” the growth agenda.  
Priority customer segments (what to double down on vs. prune): from the uploaded data our working hypothesis is that 3 segments matter most — (1) Core incumbent mid‑market accounts (high retention, above‑average margin; prioritize), (2) Growth potential accounts (mid revenue today, high NPS/potential for upsell; invest selectively), and (3) Commodity low‑margin / transactional accounts (low NPS, high churn/discount sensitivity; aggressively contain or migrate to self‑serve).  
Value‑prop & economics hypotheses (how to get 200–300 bps): near‑term levers (2–4 quarters): tighten discount governance and implement value‑based bundles for Core/Growth (expected pricing recovery 120–180 bps); migrate Commodity accounts to a lower‑cost self‑serve tier and enforce minimum contract economics (cost‑to‑serve reduction 60–90 bps); accelerate targeted upsell/cross‑sell campaigns to top 30% accounts and reduce churn via focused retention squads (adds remaining bps + topline lift).  
Capabilities, competitive position & hard tradeoffs: rapid wins require immediate fixes to pricing tools, commercial ops (segment‑based quotas & compensation), and delivery automation; tough choices management must be prepared to make this quarter include culling (or repricing) unprofitable accounts, reassigning AEs away from low‑value accounts, and funding short, sharp investments in digital onboarding and sales enablement to defend against the competitor’s discount program.  
Analyses to run in next 24–36 hours (firm methodology): clarify objectives & constraints — validate BU P&L waterfalls, target margin scenarios (200/250/300 bps) and sensitivity to churn/pricing; segment customers — re‑build segments from CRM + revenue/NPS/churn (flag top 30% by profit, bottom 30% loss‑makers), and validate latest month when CRM is cleared; value propositions & economics — margin-by-product/segment, cost‑to‑serve, price‑elasticity and win/loss analysis vs. competitor discounting, quick A/B pricing tests design; capabilities & competition — sales productivity by AE, contract/discount leakage analysis, delivery unit economics and automation gap assessment; roadmap & quantification — build 12‑ and 18‑month impact model of proposed bundle/pricing/cost levers, list quarter‑by‑quarter quick wins (discount freeze, self‑serve migration, top‑30 account retention sprints) and medium‑term transformation moves, with risks and mitigations for the board.
